rows: Golfball size hail was reported at the intersection of Texas Highways 17 and 166 southwest of Fort Davis.

Penny sized hail and heavy rain fell in downtown Fort Davis. In addition, the Presidio County Sheriff's office reported power outages in Fort Davis and Valentine. The cause of the power outage was unknown.

Quarter size hail fell at the intersection of Texas Highway 17 and Farm to Market Road 1832.
Nickel size hail fell on Texas Highway 17 on the Jeff Davis/Reeves County line.
A tornado was reported near the Buffalo Trail Boy Scout Camp north-northwest of Fort Davis.
Nickel size hail fell on the Culberson/Jeff Davis County line on Texas Highway 118.
Golfball to baseball hail fell at the intersection of Texas Highway 17 and Buffalo Trail Boy Scout Camp Road.
Golfball sized hail fell at the Buffalo Trail Boy Scout Camp.
Penny to nickel sized hail fell on Texas State Highway 166 west of Fort Davis.
Quarter sized hail covered the ground and was two inches deep. Also, trees were partially stripped of their leaves.
A 71 mph gust was measured by a trained spotter. No damage was reported.
A 62 mph wind gust was reported by the media at McDonald Observatory. No damage was reported.
A 60 mph wind gust was reported at the McDonald Observatory. No damage was reported.
Golfball sized hail fell on Texas State Highway 118, two miles south of the McDonald Observatory.
Nickel to quarter size hail fell northwest of Fort Davis.
Thunderstorm winds downed powerlines in Valentine.
A retired National Weather Service employee reported penny sized hail which lasted for six minutes.
The park ranger's windshield was broken by the hail.
One inch hail covered the ground in Valentine.
A thunderstorm moved over Jeff Davis County and produced wind damage in Valentine. A chimney and several tree branches were blown down. The cost of damage is a very rough estimate.
Hail of 1.5 inches along with strong winds and heavy rainfall was reported 6 miles west northwest of Fort Davis.
A thunderstorm moved across Jeff Davis County and produced a 65 mph wind gust at McDonald Observatory.
A thunderstorm moved across Jeff Davis County and produced a 79 mph wind gust at the McDonald Observatory.
A thunderstorm moved across Jeff Davis County and produced a 79 mph wind gust at McDonald Observatory.
A thunderstorm moved across Jeff Davis County and produced two inch hail in Fort Davis. The hail caused broken windows, skylights, and window panes. The cost of damage is a very rough estimate.
A thunderstorm moved across Jeff Davis County and produced golfball sized hail in Fort Davis. The hail shattered a vehicle window. The cost of damage is a very rough estimate.
A thunderstorm produced a 62 mph wind gust nine miles east of Kent.
A thunderstorm produced quarter sized hail ten miles southwest of McDonald Observatory. There was lots of quarter sized hail covering the ground at Bloys Camp.
A thunderstorm produced a 63 mph wind gust at the Kent Mesonet site.

Lanspout: A landspout tornado developed around 408 PM CDT about 20 miles northwest of Marfa, TX, and was on the ground for approximately one minute. A second developed shortly after the first, dissipating within 10 to 15 seconds. No damage was reported. Path details are estimates…
Half-dollar-size hail was reported near Fort Davis.
A roof was partially blown off of a shed with minor tree damage in the area. Wind speeds are estimated to have been around 70 mph. Property damage is an estimate.
One inch diameter hail was observed at McDonald Observatory.
Relayed report by broadcast media. Time estimated from radar.
Quarter to half-dollar-size hail was observed at the Davis Mountain resort.
The wind gust was measured at Fort Davis RAWS station. Time estimated from radar.
This report was received from mPING.
A storm chaser reported hail up to quarter-size covering the roadway along State Highway 17.
The West Texas Mesonet Station 13 W Toyavale measured a 64 mph wind gust.
